children.translated_text: <s>Sāmānyadūṣaṇam</s> (Refutation of Universals)

children.text: व्यापकं नित्यमेकं च सामान्यं यैः प्रकल्पितम् ।
children.translated_text: For those who have postulated a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) that is pervasive, permanent, and one,
its non-existence is here established, in order to cut the knot of their delusion.
perceived through direct perception, the accompanying form
which is the basis for the production of a cognition and a verbal expression of non-difference—[this] universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) is not to be accepted by the wise?

Because there is an absence of establishing means of valid knowledge (<s>sādhaka-pramāṇa</s>) and because there is the possibility of invalidating means of valid knowledge (<s>bādhaka-pramāṇa</s>)—so we say.
How is it understood that in [entities that are] momentary and mutually distinct,
For the inference that is stated by the opponents as the proof of universals [is as follows]:
A cognition that has a conforming aspect is grounded in a conforming object.

children.text: यथा बहुषु पुष्पेषु स्रक् स्रगिति ज्न्ँआनम् ।
children.translated_text: Just as, with respect to many garlands, there is the cognition "garland, garland."
And there is a cognition with a conforming aspect in instances such as effects and the like that are devoid of mutual contact—
since the body of that [inference] is afflicted by the fault of inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatā</s>), it is not sufficient for establishing the existence of that [universal].

children.text: यतो भवति बहुषु पाचकेषु पाचकः पाचक इति एकाकारपरामर्शप्रत्ययः ।
children.translated_text: For there arises, with respect to many cooks, the cognition of identical aspect: "cook, cook."

children.text: न च तेष्वनुगतमेकं वस्तु समस्ति । तद्भावे हि प्रागेव तथाविधप्रत्ययोत्पाद
children.translated_text: And there is no single conforming entity present in them. For if it were present, the unwelcome consequence
of such a cognition arising even prior [to any cooking activity] would be of irresistible force.
[we reply:] This is not so. Because permanent [entities], being incapable of having any excellence conferred upon them, [entail] no requirement

children.text: योगात् । सातिशयत्वे वा प्रतिक्षणं विशरारुशरीरत्वात् क्रिया कुत इति
children.translated_text: for a cooperating condition. Or, if they are subject to excellence, then since their nature would disintegrate at every moment, whence would activity arise?—
this fault is difficult to overcome. Nor is it to be maintained that the cognition of conforming aspect in cooks is not inconclusive because it is grounded in activity.

children.text: कान्तिकतादोष इत्यपि वार्तम् । प्रतिभेदं भिद्यमानानां कर्मणां तन्निबन्धनत्वा
children.translated_text: Because actions, which differ with each individual case, cannot be the ground of that [conforming cognition],

since they differ [from case to case]. And if [one says] that even different [actions] are the ground of a cognition of non-different aspect, then the same would apply to the individuals (<s>vyakti</s>) themselves—

children.text: न राजदण्डनिवारितः । ततश्च सामान्यमेव नोपेयं स्यादिति मूलहरं
children.translated_text: [and this] is not prevented by royal decree. Consequently, the universal itself would never need to be accepted—and thus the dear fool, resorting to a position that

children.text: पक्षमाश्रयता देवानांप्रियेण सुष्ठु अनुकूलमाचरितम् । अनेनैव न्यायेन क्रिया
children.translated_text: undercuts the root, has acted quite consistently. By this very reasoning, one who constructs the relation of action and agent
as the ground of non-different cognition is [also] refuted.
If [one objects that] this is not a fault because the particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), which require the assistance of activity (<s>kriyā</s>), are the revealers of the universal—

children.text: कान्तिकतादोष इत्यपि न मन्तव्यम् । न ह्यर्थान्तरसंबन्धिनी जातिरर्था
children.translated_text: subject to the fault of inconclusiveness. For a universal (<s>jāti</s>) belonging to one thing is not the cause of the production of a cognition
of another thing, because of over-extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).
Nor should one think that the cognition of conforming aspect in cooks, being grounded in the [universal of] cooking-action-ness, is not

children.text: भिन्नाकारं परामर्शप्रत्ययमुपजनयति । ततो न यथोक्तो दोषः ।
children.translated_text: generates a cognition of non-different aspect in the cooks. Therefore, the stated fault does not apply.
One might say: Through the force of the relation of inherence-in-what-is-inherent (<s>samavetasamavāya</s>), the universal of cooking-action
[their] very existence is impossible [at the time of cognition].

children.text: विनष्टे कर्मणि तत्सामान्यं न कर्मणि तदभावादेव, नापि कर्तरीति संबद्ध
children.translated_text: When the action has perished, the universal of that [action] is not in the action, since [the action] no longer exists, nor is it in the agent—thus even the connected
relation of this [universal] does not exist, and so it is not the cause of a cognition of non-difference. Therefore it stands
that this inference, being vitiated by the fault of inconclusiveness,
is not sufficient for establishing the existence of universals.
This too is without substance. Because, since actions cease immediately after arising,

children.text: इतश्चापि न सामान्यसत्तासाधनमिदमनुमानम् । यथैव हि परस्परा
सङ्कीर्णस्वभावा अपि शाबलेयादयो भावाः कयाचिदेव तदेककार्यप्रति
children.translated_text: unmixed natures, by a certain inherent nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) that comes from the force of their own causes,
characterized by a fixed correlation with one particular effect, contribute to that one [thing] deemed
as the conforming form—without requiring yet another, separate universal, since otherwise there would be an infinite regress—so too
let them
generate a single cognition of [conforming] identification. What need is there of a universal endowed with distinctness, [sitting there like] a goiter
in between?
For this further reason too, this inference does not establish the existence of universals. For just as entities such as spotted cows and the like, though of mutually
must necessarily be accepted

children.text: लापिभिरपि नियतमभ्युपगमनीयम् । अन्यथा कुतः शालिबीजं शाल्यङ्कुर
children.translated_text: even by those who deny universals. Otherwise, when one is pressed with the question "why does a rice seed produce

children.text: मेव जनयति न कोद्रवाङ्कुरमिति परपर्यनुयोगे भावप्रकृतिं मुक्त्वा किमपर
children.translated_text: only a rice sprout and not a millet sprout?"—apart from [appealing to] the nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) of things, what else
is there to be said here?
Now if it is said: All entities have fixed capacities (<s>śakti</s>). And this

मप्येवं शक्ता एव वक्तुम् । सामान्यमेवोपकर्तुं शक्तिर्व्यक्तीनां भेदाविशेषेऽपि
children.translated_text: are able to say exactly this: The capacity of the individuals (<s>vyakti</s>) is only to assist the universal, and even in the absence of difference [among them],
[they lack the capacity] to generate that single cognition.
This reply is not devoured by the denizens of the forest [i.e., not invalidated] for us either. For we too
and yet you do not perceive it
yourself! For when the cause-and-effect relation between a rice seed and its sprout is ascertained on the basis of direct perception and non-apprehension,

children.text: कार्यकारणभावेऽवगते शालिबीजं शाल्यङ्कुरं जनयितुं शक्तं न कोद्रवाङ्कुर
children.translated_text: one can say that the rice seed is capable of producing a rice sprout and not a millet
sprout. But the benefactor-beneficiary relation between the universal and its possessor is not ascertained
from any means of valid knowledge whatsoever. So how can this reply, when offered, carry any
weight? Enough with this insistence on what is false! Merely from the absence of establishing evidence, the discerning do not
engage in the practice of treating as non-existent. Therefore, listen to the inference we state that establishes the non-existence of that [universal].
What an unanswerable predicament of faults you are being led into by your defective vision,
as non-existent.

Like a sky-lotus.
non-apprehension of [an entity's own] nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s>).

भवन्ती स्वरूपतो विशेषणतो वा भवेत् ? तत्र न तावदाद्या

is not possible,
because non-apprehension, which has the form of apprehending something else, is accepted [by both parties]. And since its own form is directly known through self-cognition (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>),
through the direct perception of <s>svasaṃvedana</s>, how is there scope for the fault of non-establishment of its own form?
Nor should one counter this by raising the fault of non-establishment (<s>asiddhi</s>). For, here, would the non-establishment

तयैवासिधारया सैवासिधारा च्छिद्यते; तदेवाङ्गुल्यग्रं तेनैवाङ्गुल्यग्रेण स्पृश्यत
children.translated_text: is a sword-blade cut by that very sword-blade, nor is a fingertip touched by that very fingertip—
and therefore this reason is simply unestablished,
[we reply:] this only reveals that the words are a display of ignorance
of the meaning of the term <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-cognition).
If it is said that self-cognition (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) itself is not possible, because of the contradiction of an action directed upon itself—for neither

not depending on another cognition, while being luminous, is called its own illuminator.
For cognition arises as distinguished from pots, blue lotuses, and the like. Therefore,
truth: cognition is not established as being cognized by another cognition, nor is it said

children.text: संविदितमुच्यते । यथा प्रकारे च स्वसंवेदनशब्दार्थे विवक्षिते न किन्ँचिद्

to be said [against it]—so whence the scope for the stated fault?
Therefore, this is the ultimate

with respect to something,
[when] that [basis] is not a mark of that [thing], the cognition of that does not arise—like [the cognition of] a staff-bearer [where there is no staff].
Nor should the non-establishment due to non-establishment of the qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>) be raised. Because the opponents themselves accept
has put forth:
"Do you cognize the universal or not?

children.translated_text: then what other persisting form (<s>anugatākāra</s>) belongs to the <s>sāmānya</s> (universal)? If you ask this,

children.text: ननु वर्णसंस्थाने विरहय्य किमपरमनुगामि विद्यते ? जातिव्यक्त्योः समवाय
children.translated_text: well, setting aside color and configuration, what other persisting [entity] exists? If you say: the apprehension of genus and particular, whose distinction is unperceived due to the force of inherence (<s>samavāya</s>),
is through mutual intermixture, like milk and water —

children.text: चेत् ? न तर्हि सामान्यविशेषयोरेकतरस्यापि रूपं गृहीतम् । स्वरूपाग्रहणे
children.translated_text: then the form of neither the universal nor the particular has been grasped. When the intrinsic nature is not grasped,

children.text: अनयोरप्यग्रहणमिति निरालम्बनैव सा तादृशी प्रतिपत्तिरिति परमार्थ आवे
children.translated_text: there is no grasping of either of these two — thus such a cognition is without a real basis (<s>nirālambana</s>). This is the ultimate truth that has been

children.text: दितस्तावत् । निरालम्बनया च प्रतीत्या व्यवस्थाप्यमानं सामान्यं सुव्यव
children.translated_text: revealed. And a <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) that is established by a cognition without real basis is indeed well
established [i.e., not established at all, spoken ironically]!
Nor is <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal), like the configuration of a [real] entity,
Therefore, even through the unestablishedness of the qualificand (<s>viśeṣya</s>), this reason is not unestablished.

children.text: सपक्षे वर्तमानो विरुद्ध इत्यपि न मन्तव्यः ।
children.translated_text: Nor should it be thought that [the reason], being present in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (positive example), is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>).
The inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatā</s>) of this [reason] too does not merit consideration.

children.text: असद्व्यवहारानपेक्षत्वेन हि दृश्यानुपलम्भो व्याप्तः । यदि हि सन्नपि
तत्र न प्रवर्तयेत्, इह सापेक्षः स्यात् । ततो विपक्षाद् व्यापकविरुद्धावरुद्धाद्
children.translated_text: [perception] were not to function there, then here it would be dependent. Therefore, being excluded from the counter-example, which is blocked by the contradictory of the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddha</s>),
[the reason] comes to rest in the conventional usage of non-existence. Thus, non-perception is pervaded by that conventional usage of non-existence —

children.text: व्याप्त इति कुतोऽनेकान्तः ? ततश्च स एवार्थः समायातः ।
children.translated_text: so from where would there be inconclusiveness? And thus the same conclusion has been reached.

And the ultimate meaning of everything stated above is this:
In the five fingers that appear in perceptual manifestation, no

children.text: सामान्यं प्रतिभासते न च विकल्पाकारबुद्धौ तथा ।
children.translated_text: <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) appears as established; nor does it so appear in conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpākārabuddhi</s>).
not a <s>jāti</s> (genus); therefore
It is those very [fingers] with indistinct forms that appear here —
these two — the cause of the illusion of similarity (<s>sādṛśyabhrama</s>) — are [merely] the resonances of a single apprehension.
Thus the direction of the refutation of the establishment of universals (<s>Sāmānyasiddhidūṣaṇā</s>) has been demonstrated.
This is the composition of the learned <s>Aśoka</s>.
